m01.title: The Fruit of the Ground
m01.desc: Cain was a tiller of the ground. He brings of its fruit as an offering.

steps.gather: Gather the fruit of your field ({n}/{total})
steps.altar: Bring your offering to the altar

m02.title: The Firstlings of the Flock
m02.desc: Abel was a keeper of sheep. He brings the firstlings of his flock and their fat.

steps.fold: Bring the flock into the fold ({n}/{total})
steps.altar: Bring the fat to the altar

m03.title: The Two Offerings
m03.desc: The LORD looks on the two offerings.

m04.title: In the Field
m04.desc: Cain talks with Abel his brother, and they go out to the field.

steps.field: Go out to your field with Abel
steps.jawbone: Take the jawbone lying in the field
steps.chase: Catch Abel before he reaches his father and mother

steps.east: Go away east, out of the land

born.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD.

keeper.text: And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

firstlings.text: And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof.

respect.text: And the LORD had respect unto Abel and to his offering: but unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect.

wroth.text: And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.

slew.text: And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

mark.text: And the LORD set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

nod.text: And Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

command.t: Cain, Abel. Bring me an offering, each of you, from the work of your hands.
I will bring the fruit of my field.
And I, the firstlings of my flock.

herd.t: Come, boy! Bring them in to the fold.

rebuke.t: Why are you angry? Why has your face fallen?
If you do well, will you not be accepted? If not, sin lies at the door. It wants you, but you must rule over it.

field.t: Abel. Come with me, let us go out to the field.

fear.t: Cain? What are you doing with that?

where.t: I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?
What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood cries to me from the ground.
When you till the ground, it will no longer give you its strength. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.
My punishment is greater than I can bear. Whoever finds me will kill me.
Not so. Whoever kills Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.

before: I worked the ground by the sweat of my brow. Now my sons work it with me.
Bring the LORD your best, my son.
We could not go back to the garden. But the LORD has not left us.
Cain keeps the field, Abel keeps the sheep. Each has his work.
after: The LORD looked on your brother's offering. Do not let your heart grow dark.
Anger is a heavy thing to carry, son. Put it down.
Where is your brother? He should be home before the evening.

before: I have gotten a man from the LORD. And then another. My two sons.
The pot is almost ready. Go on, do your work first.
Take care of your brother, Cain.
The tunics the LORD made us still keep us warm.
after: Your face has fallen, Cain. What is it?
Make peace with your brother before the sun goes down.
Is Abel with you? I have kept his bread warm.

hints.herd: Now you are the dog. Run round behind the sheep and drive them gently through the gate.

prompts.offer: Lay the offering on the altar

chase.escaped: Abel reached his father and mother. Try again.

complete.body: Cain went out from the presence of the LORD to the land of Nod. But Abel's offering was not forgotten: by faith he offered a more excellent sacrifice (Hebrews 11:4).
complete.next: Next on the path: Noah and the Flood.
